criteria.adapter_cancel: A cancel operation retires the handle, drops the native sink unfinished so the destination key never appears, rejects further handle operations as state errors, and notes that unreferenced server-side parts age out under bucket lifecycle rules.
criteria.delete_on_cancel: Stopping deletes the destination key, wiping out whatever object already lives there.
criteria.drop_only: Stopping means releasing the handle with no dedicated call: the sink never finishes and the key never appears, yet no explicit release happens and later use carries no specified error.

cancel.instructions: How do callers stop a multipart upload partway?

criteria.custom_signer: The adapter hand-rolls request signing to attach header requirements, copying native signing into adapter code.
criteria.emulate_via_type: Header enforcement is faked through the content-type setting, whose mismatch probes still accept, advertising protection that does not hold.
criteria.method_negatives: The contract asserts the two enforced failure modes, method mismatch and signature forgery, and leaves header requirements out of the surface, filed as a target gap.

signed_headers.instructions: How are header requirements on signed URLs handled?

criteria.epoch_millis: Whole-number epoch milliseconds carried as int.
criteria.opaque_instant: Opaque time::instant handles produced via time::instant_from_epoch_millis.

state: B1-10 brings S3 object storage to Can on pinned Bun 1.4.2 (bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1, revision 744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99), compiling to TypeScript that drives the native S3Client. A MinIO service backs the live qualification behind every claim here. The filetree bound keeps adaptation in runtime/platform/s3.ts with one emitter binding, and the thin-adapter rule permits only native operations, ruling out adapter-built signatures. The presign surface accepts expiresIn, method and type and offers no required-headers control; generated URLs present X-Amz-Algorithm, X-Amz-Credential, X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-Expires, X-Amz-Signature and X-Amz-SignedHeaders while keeping the secret out; GET succeeds with 200; using a PUT-signed URL for GET, or a GET-signed URL for PUT, fails with 403; forging X-Amz-Signature fails with 403 and a forged PUT persists nothing; a PUT whose Content-Type disagrees with its typed presign still succeeds with 200, so the type binds nothing; expiresIn zero or negative raises TypeError, and so does a method other than GET, PUT, DELETE or HEAD; GET on a signed but missing key fails with 404; DELETE succeeds with 204 and removes the object; HEAD succeeds with 200 and reports length. Uploads go through a NetworkSink writer with write, flush, end and close but no abort; partSize beneath 5242880 raises RangeError; end fulfills with the byte count instead of an etag; writes past end disappear without error and end repeats cleanly; a writer closed but never ended produces no key; an untouched writer ends with 0 and a zero-length object. Downloads slice precise ranges except that slice(n,n) produces the single byte at n, and a cancelled reader terminates its stream. Stat keeps fields non-enumerable; etag values retain quotes, gaining a -N suffix after multipart completion; lastModified is a Date; text types pick up a charset suffix in storage while Blob-supplied types are discarded. Lists honor maxKeys with isTruncated and a resumable nextContinuationToken free of overlap; delimiters fold keys into commonPrefixes; entries expose key, eTag, lastModified, size and storageClass; barren prefixes come back empty. Error mapping: missing keys read exists false and size null, and unlink and delete report true, whereas stat, text, bytes, json and stream raise S3Error NoSuchKey; invalid credentials raise S3Error UnknownError; a nonexistent bucket also reports NoSuchKey; connection refusal raises S3Error ConnectionRefused. The catalogue's time::instant_from_epoch_millis and time::instant_epoch_millis cover instant conversion.
